pr.title: Set up a required Projector review check from project init
pr.head: f7ecc2602d94a9d5967d91e45b9a77037f73020d

summary: Projector reviews a pull request and, after this stack, signs off a clean head with a clean label and, where the default branch requires it, a projector/review commit status. A status blocks a merge only once a GitHub ruleset requires it. This pull request, the top layer of the stack, lets project init set that requirement up for a repository that relies on Projector alone to sign off pull requests.

At a terminal, in a GitHub repository whose default branch does not require projector/review yet, init asks one yes-or-no question. --require-review and --no-require-review answer it without a prompt, and without a terminal or a flag init asks nothing. A yes does four things in order:

1. Creates the ruleset. The Projector review ruleset requires projector/review on the default branch with no bypass. When GitHub refuses, for lack of admin access or a paid plan on a private repository, init exits non-zero and does nothing else.
  2. Writes the label workflow. .github/workflows/projector-clean.yml takes clean off a pull request when a commit is pushed to it. init skips it while review.labels is false.
  3. Backfills the status. It posts success on each open pull request whose current head a review already signed off, so none is blocked on a review it has.
  4. Records the answer. review.require_check = true goes into the repository's .projector.toml.

A no records false, and init stops asking. A recorded yes puts back a missing ruleset or workflow. The layer also records the plan's end-to-end check and marks the review-on-ready plan completed, because it carries the project's last code.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Ruleset: a set of GitHub branch rules; this one requires a commit status before a merge.
  • projector/review: the commit status context that project review publish posts on a reviewed head.
  • Signed off: the newest counted Projector verdict on the head is clean, and no Projector finding thread is open.
  • review.require_check: the recorded answer to init's question. Unset asks at a terminal, true keeps the setup in place, and false asks no more.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: One Projector review, at f7ecc26, requested changes with one finding: plain project init at a terminal now exits non-zero when gh cannot read the default branch's rules. It also suggested two smaller changes, about a failed backfill and about --require-review outside a repository.

groups.title: The question and the setup in init
groups.kicker: How init decides whether to ask, and what a yes writes to GitHub and the checkout
intro: init_required_check in cli.py runs after init's other steps. It reads the answer from the flags and from review.require_check, returns early when there is no person to ask and nothing recorded, reads the default branch's rules, and asks only when the branch does not already require the check.

The GitHub side lives in review.py beside the constants publish uses: ruleset() builds the ruleset body from REVIEW_CONTEXT, create_ruleset posts it, clean_workflow_text fills the template with CLEAN_LABEL, and backfill_statuses counts each open pull request's verdicts with sign_off, as project review status does.

checks.text: A refused ruleset raises InitError before the backfill, the workflow, and the setting, so a refusal leaves no partial setup. A failure after the ruleset exists, in the backfill, is not caught the same way.

files.note: The flags, the question, and init_required_check with its helpers for the setting and the workflow file.

checks.text: Open finding: at a terminal, with the setting unset and no flag, a failed read of the rules, such as gh missing, signed out, or offline, becomes an InitError, so plain project init exits 65 where the base exits 0. The site step turns the same failure into a note. The fix is to skip the question with a note unless a flag or a recorded true asked for the check.
Reproduced with the repository's own test harness, a GitHub origin, a terminal, and a failing gh: init --no-site --no-publish-rule exits 65 at this head and 0 at the base.

files.note: The ruleset body, its creation, the workflow text, and the status backfill, built from the label and context constants publish already uses.

The workflow init writes. It runs on pull_request_target so it can edit a fork's pull request, never checks out the pull request's code, and its job-level if skips the run unless the label is present.
Ships templates/*.yml in the wheel, so an installed project can read the workflow template.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: A fake GitHub for the question, the flags, the refusal, and the backfill
intro: RequiredCheckTests runs init in a temporary repository whose origin is acme/app, with run_gh replaced by RulesetGitHub, a fake that keeps the rules, the rulesets, the open pull requests with their verdicts, and the statuses posted. The site's init tests now run without a terminal, so they never meet the question.

checks.text: The full suite at this head ran 1229 tests, OK with 1 skipped, and RequiredCheckTests ran 9 tests, OK.

files.note: Nine tests: a yes and a later run, a no, no terminal, a refused ruleset, labels off, a branch that already requires the check, a recorded yes with the ruleset gone, and a workflow edited by hand.
Patches isatty to false in the site's init helper, so those tests run as an agent runs init.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: The living docs for the question, and the plan's outcome
intro: docs/cli.md gains a section on requiring a clean review before merge and a row for review.require_check in the settings table. The plan gains § 9.3, what implementation settled about the setup, and § 10, the outcome with the end-to-end check run in a public scratch repository, and moves from in-progress to completed.
